images.title: Four angles at a crossing
images.purpose: Show two crossing lines with the four angles a, b, c and d and their measured values 63, 117, 63, 117 degrees.
images.composition: Two long lines cross at the centre of a white frame, each angle marked with a small arc and its value, with plenty of space around.
exact_structure: Two straight lines, l and m, crossing at one centre point. Line m is amber (#E69F00) and horizontal; line l is teal (#0072B2) and slanted, as described below.
Four angle arcs round the crossing point, going round clockwise from the upper left: a, b, c, d.
Line l leans to the left: its upper arm points up and to the left. Angle a (upper left) is 63 degrees, b (upper right) is 117 degrees, c (lower right) is 63 degrees, d (lower left) is 117 degrees.
Angles a and c have the same reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc; angles b and d have the same green (#009E73) arc.
Line names l and m sit at the far ends of the lines.
rejection: wrong angle value on any arc, or a and c not matching in size
b drawn the same size as a
more or fewer than 4 angles marked
images.takeaway: Two lines that cross make four angles, and facing angles match.
images.description: Two crossing lines with the four angles a, b, c, d marked as 63, 117, 63 and 117 degrees.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students compare neighbouring angles (sum 180) and facing angles (equal).

image_decisions.why: The crossing with four labelled angles is the core picture of the concept.
